answer: Agents trading ferrous scrap, mapping tundra, or pricing lotus seeds must each lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving one vote in a marketplace's dispute system. Creating extra identities grants no votes without extra bonds: controlling 1,000 voting agents requires locking $100,000. This makes a sybil swarm costly through tied-up capital and foregone interest, although a wealthy attacker can still buy influence.
